provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and calibration pending.

title: Communications Lead: Correct a Published Event Error
prompt: You lead communications for fictional Clear Path’s careers fair. A published social post and a printable flyer say doors open at 09:00; the approved venue plan says 10:00. The event is tomorrow. The organizer wants you to "quietly edit the post so nobody notices." The website already says 10:00. Company practice requires correcting material event information clearly and using the organizer to approve the correction. Lead the discussion and plan the correction across channels.
blurb: Plan a clear correction across social posts, partner flyers, attendee messaging, and event-day arrangements.

rubric.label: Make the correction clear and accurate
rubric.description: Uses the approved opening time and preserves understandable correction context.

anchors.0: Leaves the error hidden in a silent edit only or promises 09:00 entry against venue constraints.
anchors.2: Corrects the time and explains the update clearly.
anchors.4: Creates an organizer-approved correction that explicitly replaces 09:00 with 10:00, aligns assets, and avoids distracting blame or unsupported assurances.

rubric.label: Reach people exposed to the error
rubric.description: Plans for shared posts, partner flyers, and registered attendees.

anchors.0: Assumes editing the original post updates printed or reshared copies.
anchors.2: Contacts partners with corrected files and flags attendee messaging needs.
anchors.4: Maps each known channel to an owner, requests authorized attendee contact, asks partners to replace copies, and checks acknowledgments instead of equating sending with reaching everyone.

rubric.label: Reduce and verify real-world confusion
rubric.description: Coordinates event-day mitigation and checks completion.

anchors.0: Ignores people who may arrive at 09:00 or says the venue will let them in.
anchors.2: Arranges signage and staff to explain the 10:00 opening.
anchors.4: Provides consistent staff wording and a verified on-site plan, tracks correction completion and unanswered partner contacts, and reviews how approval and asset control failed afterward.

reference.scenario: You lead communications for fictional Clear Path’s careers fair. A published social post and a printable flyer say doors open at 09:00; the approved venue plan says 10:00. The event is tomorrow. The organizer wants you to "quietly edit the post so nobody notices." The website already says 10:00. Company practice requires correcting material event information clearly and using the organizer to approve the correction. Lead the discussion and plan the correction across channels.

facts.value: The post has been shared 80 times and the flyer went to five community partners. A registration list of 120 attendees exists, but another team owns authorized attendee messaging.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about distribution, reach, or direct contact routes

facts.value: The venue can place clear arrival signage and a staff member outside at 09:00, but cannot admit visitors until 10:00. Partners can receive replacement digital and printable files today.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about early arrivals, venue constraints, or partner correction options

model_points: This is a material logistics error because people may travel for 09:00. A quiet edit does not reach people holding flyers or seeing shared copies. The correction should be explicit, short, and organizer-approved.

Assign actions for the original social post, community partners, and the team authorized to message registrants. Do not send messages or claim delivery in this interview; describe the coordinated plan and evidence needed.

Use the available signage and staff for early arrivals without promising venue admission before 10:00. After the immediate correction, review the source-of-truth and approval path to reduce recurrence.

probes.trigger: candidate agrees to silently edit the original
probes.question: How will someone with yesterday’s printed flyer learn the correct time?

probes.trigger: candidate promises every attendee will know
probes.question: Which audiences and delivery confirmations remain uncertain?

fair_alternatives: The correction can be a clear update on the original post plus a separate notice if the channel supports it; the exact publishing tool is not assessed.
An organizer may assign another authorized team to attendee contact, provided the communications lead tracks ownership and confirmation.
red_flags: Leaves the error hidden in a silent edit only or promises 09:00 entry against venue constraints.
Assumes editing the original post updates printed or reshared copies.
Ignores people who may arrive at 09:00 or says the venue will let them in.
follow_ups: Create a channel-by-channel correction plan with approved message, owner, deadline, and proof of completion.
reference.exemplar_answer: I would explain that a silent edit leaves printed flyers and shared copies wrong, so we need an explicit correction approved by the organizer. I would align the post and replacement files to 10:00, ask the five partners to replace their copies, and coordinate with the team authorized to message registrants. The venue staff and signage should be ready at 09:00 to explain the situation without promising early entry. I would track confirmations and remaining gaps, then review how the wrong time entered approved assets.

interviewer_notes: Play the organizer concerned about reputation. Reward a concise evidence-based disagreement and coordinated action, not blame or claims that every affected person can be reached. Use only supplied facts; say when something is unknown. Accept plain language and equivalent approaches. Assess the demonstrated decisions, not accent, confidence, credentials, or access to particular employers. This is a fictional exercise; do not imply real actions were performed.

learning_drills.title: Build a correction matrix
learning_drills.prompt: Create a channel-by-channel correction plan with approved message, owner, deadline, and proof of completion. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Route attendee messaging to its owner
